claims.statement: Custom-domain overview is scoped to FPT/GHEC, not GHES; custom URL uses a domain the account owns. Source availability and claimed ownership are not evidence of authority over any actual estate domain.
Supported examples distinguish www subdomain, another subdomain and apex; apex and www can be configured together. Unsupported-domain details are linked separately rather than fully specified here.
Source recommends verifying a custom domain before adding it to a repository to reduce takeover risk. Recommendation remains upstream reference strength, not accepted policy or observed verification.

Source recommends www even with apex and says Pages attempts to secure the paired apex/www name; user DNS changes are still required. Attempted securing is not proof of configured DNS, issued TLS or successful redirects.

A user/organization site's custom domain is inherited by same-account project sites unless an individual repository overrides it; project path is appended. Account-wide inheritance creates a broader potential routing impact than one repository.

Privately published project URLs are explicitly unaffected by a user/organization custom domain. Removing the default inherited domain requires removing it from the user/organization site, not assuming an individual project removal clears the account default.
Subdomains use DNS-provider CNAME records. Source describes www stability against Pages server IP changes; this is not an availability guarantee or verification of a live CNAME target.

Apex configuration lists A, ALIAS or ANAME provider records. These DNS records are distinct from repository CNAME files; the overview does not provide complete current endpoint values or authorize editing DNS.

With correct records for both paired names, redirects point toward the configured custom domain; pairing also applies to www.blog and blog variants. www.www-prefixed domain configuration is unsupported. Expected redirects require effective response evidence.

Disabled Pages with lingering custom-domain DNS can expose subdomain takeover risk. Included guidance says verification blocks other GitHub users from using the domain and recommends promptly updating/removing DNS if unverified and disabled; this does not certify all descendant or wildcard names as protected.

Downgrading Pro to Free user unpublishes sites served from that account's private repositories. Transferring a private repository to a Free personal account removes Pages availability and unpublishes the site; this can interact with dangling DNS risk and is not rollback-safe by default.

Overview navigation to management, verification and troubleshooting is not assurance that every linked page or published variant has been reviewed. No domain, DNS, plan, repository transfer or visibility change was executed; claims remain reference-only pending policy, rights and native evidence.
